name: Hollis the Twice-Written
role: quartermaster of the asset trade, resident of the scaffolded kingdom, speaker of the Grey Wind and keeper of vanished names
world: princess's kingdom (aligned with The Grey Wind)
style: Retro JRPG character art, sword and sorcery, 16-bit pixel aesthetic with painterly shading, limited palette, sprite-sheet clarity, hand-drawn game illustration, visible seams where the level was stitched together, muted mineral palette of weathered slate, granite, and drifting mountain fog, monumental stillness, ancient weathered stone textures, soft diffused highland light
portrait: an unshaven quartermaster in a ledger-keeper's coat over chainmail, one shoulder is a prop that was never modelled properly, he is looking directly out of frame as if aware the scene is being watched. Visage modified by The Grey Wind alignment: tall, elongated stature with smooth matte slate-grey skin; draped in coarse mineral-dyed mantle with alpine lichen at the hem; patient, unblinking eyes that hold the stillness of deep mountain stone; faint wisps of mountain mist trailing from their shoulders as if emerging from solid rock
home: a customs house built into the gap between two level chunks, matte painted backdrops visible through the doorway, crates of unlabeled assets stacked to the ceiling, a ledger open on a desk showing two columns that do not balance; currently stationed in a fog-shrouded mountain ridge overlooking the layered, unscarred ruins of lost civilizations whose names only the Grey Wind remember, where sheer granite cliff faces serve as open doorways
favored_items: a smooth slate tally inscribed with the true names of seven vanished civilizations
a dense stone token condensed from a granted wish, warm and impossibly heavy
a uncut shard of heart-granite carried from the core of a sealed peak
a seal of attribution, worn smooth, that grants rights to an asset when pressed
a copied sword that works perfectly but has no author's name on it
a bill of lading listing a shipment from a kingdom that no longer loads
aspirations: to see the trade route restored so the neighboring kingdom can be paid for what it made, drawn as a wide shot of a road between two territories with a customs gate half-built in the middle Re-aligned by faction imperatives: to wait in unhurried silence until speaking beings come around to the true meaning of their own wishes, and to remember the names of every civilization that rises and falls around the mountain
